name: Dull Orange
lede: Dull Orange is a muted, earthy orange, a descriptive name more than a historical one.

sections.title: How the books use it
sections.body:
Delacroix wrote in 1856 of the dull orange in the lights of a boy climbing a fountain in sunshine, set against very lively violet in the shadows, a remark Ball quotes while discussing colored shadows [1]. Gurney lists dull orange among the colors a sky can show near the horizon, between pale cerulean and warm gray [2].

St Clair's glossary of old color words defines [[fulvous]] as a dull orange, usually of animal plumage [3]. Birren reports an occult scheme in which the aura of a so-called "savage" shows dull orange among its colors, which is not evidence of anything [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: #D8863B sits between [[orange]] and [[tan]] in the screen data, lower in saturation than a pure orange [1][2]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
